text:
maria: Heads up — we prototyped a 'safety-sweeper' daemon that runs post-canary for 30m to detect slow-burn regressions and auto-cutover if signals persist. Want feedback on operator expectations.
aj: Nice. Is this in addition to the existing canary controller or replacing parts of it?
devon: It's an augment. Canary controller does quick checks during rollout; sweeper is a longer-lived process that looks for regressions that are not obvious in the first 5m.
maria: Exactly. Design goals: (1) minimal blast radius, (2) deterministic decision surface we can audit, (3) reversible with a single operator action.
oncall-bot: Incident policy reminder: auto-cutover must trigger a PagerDuty alert with runbook link and operator ack window >= 2m.
nate: Quick Q: what signals are we trusting? latency p50/p95, error-rate, model-quality evals?
maria: All of the above, with weights. Primary signals: request_error_rate (service), p95_latency, model_token_diff (embed/semantics drift), and eval_alerts from our evals system. Thresholds are config-driven per-customer.
selina: How do we avoid flapping between variants if signals are noisy?
devon: Sweeper keeps a short state machine: STABLE -> CONCERN (collect additional samples with higher scrutiny) -> ESCALATE (notify + reduce traffic to canary) -> CUTOVER if persisted. It requires 3 consecutive windows of anomaly of decreasing magnitude before CUTOVER.
maria: Also have a cooldown period after cutover to avoid immediate re-introductions; operator can override cooldown with a reason string.
aj: Can we see the config shape?
maria: protoconfig idea:
```json
{"sweeper_window_sec": 300, "consecutive_windows": 3, "signals": [{"name":"p95_latency","threshold_ms":1200,"weight":0.4},{"name":"error_rate","threshold_pct":0.5,"weight":0.4},{"name":"semantic_shift","threshold":0.25,"weight":0.2}], "cutover_score": 0.7, "cooldown_sec": 1800}
```
selina: Looks reasonable. Where does the sweeper run? control plane or customer infra for Private deployments?
maria: Default: control plane for hosted & dedicated. For Private, we ship a lightweight agent that posts signed decisions to the control plane. Decision logs are always pushed to customer S3/ELK if configured.
nate: What about safety for regulated customers who need manual approval?
devon: We support mode: auto, assisted, manual. Assisted mode auto-reduces traffic to 10% and opens an approval ticket (SAML SSO link). Manual requires a human to approve any cutover.
aj: Observability — need end-to-end trace IDs for sweeper decisions and sample anchors. Without that it's impossible to reconstruct.
maria: Yup — every decision includes a decision_id, query sample ids, and a minimal diff payload. We also emit a compact signature used for audits.
oncall-bot: Deploy will run tomorrow at 03:00 UTC. Reminder: add feature-flag for 'sweeper-enabled' per org.
selina: One last thought — make the scoring interpretable. Provide a breakdown so SREs can quickly see which signal pushed it over the threshold.
maria: Agreed. UX will show per-signal contribution + top 5 affected routes. I'll add that to the PR. Thanks all. :thumbsup:
